title: Belafonte's TV show with Ellington segments and pre-recorded piano
summary: Jones wrote the Ellington segments for Harry Belafonte's TV special, recorded with Hank Jones, while Duke clowned on camera.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: No, I don't think so. But -- and Duke liked it, you know. And then I did quite a bit of work with Harry Belafonte, and Ellington was -- I think we called it, "The Strolling '20s." It was a big TV show.

And I did all of the Ellington -- in fact I did most of the writing on that, on that show, and all of the Ellington sides -- Ellington segments. It was -- oh, I don't know, I guess it was Rockin' in Rhythm and a whole lot of things that I did, you know? "Drop Me Off In Harlem."

Yeah, it was a good show. I thought it was, and I was happy to be associated with it. And Duke and I began to -- oh, I remember, because Harry had wanted me to -- I had to be an ambassador for Belafonte. He says, "With everybody that I'm getting on this show you've written for." Joe Williams, Gloria Lynn, Duke Ellington. And I went to see Duke, he was recording once out in Long Island, New York, you know, and I spoke to him and I said that -- about this television show, you know. So we pre-recorded it, and we had a very good band, you know. We had all the New York heavyweights at that point. So Duke came in and he was very funny, very comical. He says, "What do you want me to do?" I says, "You don't have to do anything. Hank Jones and I have recorded you
already." So they just -- the cameras just caught him from the chest up. They never showed his hands, because we were playing.

Yeah. Duke wasn't playing. So I said, "Ellington, all you have to do is a little clowning and macking (PHONETIC)." This was what we called clowning. Because he was throwing lines back and forth with Diahann Carroll at that point. He says, "Oh, you mean I don't have to worry about the piano?" I said, "No, it's all done." And we had a lot of fun on that show. But he called me, oh, from Canada. He was doing a Shakespearean play, to conduct my people.
